## Question

Can a simple physics model of a house's heat balance, plus a small neural network that
learns what the physics misses, predict indoor temperature better than either one alone,
and stay sensible in weather it has never seen?

## Data

**REFIT Smart Home dataset** (Firth et al., Loughborough University, 2017;
[doi:10.17028/rd.lboro.2070091](https://doi.org/10.17028/rd.lboro.2070091), CC BY 4.0).
Twenty homes near Loughborough, UK, monitored from October 2013 to April 2015.

| What | Detail | Used as |
|---|---|---|
| Room air temperature | Every room, 15 or 30 min | `t_in`: volume-weighted average of heated rooms |
| Gas meter | m³ per 30 min | `q_heat` (kW): gas × 11.2 kWh/m³ × 85% boiler efficiency |
| Campus weather station | Air temp, horizontal solar, wind; 15 min; next to the homes | `t_out`, `i_sol` |
| Building survey | Room sizes, wall type, age, boiler | Context and sanity checks on R and C |

Everything is resampled to 30-minute steps. We use the **winter before the smart-home
kit was installed (4 Nov 2013 to 31 Mar 2014)**, when heating was run the usual way.

**Home choice.** `refit_data.home_coverage()` ranks the homes by how complete their
data is that winter. Four homes are 98 to 99.7% complete: **Building01** (main home,
detached 1970s cavity-wall house, 10 heated rooms), Building08 and Building07 (similar
houses, used to check the method carries over), and Building02. Building03 and
Building05 have no gas data that winter, so they are out.

The raw data is about 100 MB zipped (1.3 GB unzipped), so it is **not stored in this
repo**. `refit_data.download_refit()` downloads it into `data/refit/` (git-ignored).

**Known limitations.** Gas also heats hot water and sometimes cooking, so `q_heat`
over-counts space heating; the house is treated as one zone; 2013/14 was a mild winter
(coldest week averaged about 4.7 °C). These are exactly the gaps the neural-network
residual is there to absorb, and the write-up should say so.

## Approach

| Model | What it is | Why include it |
|---|---|---|
| Physics only | 1R1C ODE: `C dT/dt = (T_out - T_in)/R + Q_heat + a·I_sol` | Interpretable baseline. R and C mean something physical. |
| ML only | Small MLP on the same inputs | Black-box baseline |
| Hybrid | 1R1C + NN residual term, trained end to end in PyTorch | The point of the project |

**Split (Building01, 30-min steps):**

| Set | Dates | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Train | 4 Nov to 31 Dec 2013 | Two months of ordinary winter |
| Validation | 1 to 19 Jan 2014 | Tuning, early stopping |
| Test | 20 Jan to 2 Feb 2014 | Includes the coldest week of that winter (about 4.7 °C average) |
| Extra test | March 2014 | Milder and sunnier: does the model hold up in different weather? |

A first check (Nov to Dec fit, physics only) gives R ≈ 5 °C/kW and C ≈ 10 kWh/°C for
Building01, which is about 200 W/K of heat loss: sensible for a 1970s detached house.
That fit is about 0.8 °C RMSE, so there is room for the hybrid to improve on it.

## Plan: 2 weeks, Nov 17 to Dec 1, 2026

Assumes about 1 to 2 hours on weeknights and a longer block on weekends.
Thanksgiving is built in as a buffer.

### Week 1: data and baselines

| Day | Task | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Tue 11/17 – Wed 11/18 | **Setup in Positron.** Open the repo folder, create a virtual environment (`python -m venv .venv`), pick it as the interpreter, run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Run `rc_model.py`. | Synthetic fit prints |
| Thu 11/19 | **Get REFIT.** In Positron's console, from `projects/rc-thermal-hybrid/`: `import refit_data as r`, then `r.download_refit()` (~100 MB) and `r.extract_subset()` (~1 min, makes a small `refit_subset.pkl`). Run `r.home_coverage()`. | Coverage table; Building01 near the top |
| Fri 11/20 | **Look at the data.** `df = r.load_home("Building01")`. Plot a week of `t_in`, `t_out` and `q_heat` together; plot each room's temperature. Then `r.clean_for_model(df)` and make the train/validation/test split above. | Figure 1: a week of real data |
| Sat 11/21 | **Physics baseline.** Fit R, C, a_sol on train (`dt_h=0.5`). Simulate the test fortnight, plot predicted vs actual. Compare R with the building survey. | Figure 2 + table 1 |
| Sun 11/22 | **ML baseline.** Small MLP in PyTorch predicting next-step `t_in` from (`t_in`, `t_out`, `q_heat`, `i_sol`, hour of day). Evaluate 24-hour rollouts on test. | Test RMSE for ML-only |

### Week 2: hybrid model and write-up

| Day | Task | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 11/23 | **Hybrid model, part 1.** PyTorch module: Euler step with learnable R, C, a_sol (initialised from Saturday's fit) plus a small NN residual term. | Model trains without errors |
| Tue 11/24 | **Hybrid model, part 2.** Train on 24-hour rollouts, add weight decay on the NN, tune lightly on validation. | Test RMSE for hybrid |
| Wed 11/25 | **Evaluation.** RMSE table for all 3 models on the test fortnight and March. Plot the NN residual by hour of day (does it look like occupancy, cooking and hot-water use?). Repeat the physics and hybrid fits on Building08 and Building07. | Figures 3–4 + table 2 |
| Thu 11/26 – Fri 11/27 | **Thanksgiving buffer.** Catch up only if behind. | |
| Sat 11/28 | **Write-up, part 1.** Fill in Data, Approach, Results on this page. Code chunks import from `refit_data.py` and `rc_model.py`. | Page renders in `quarto preview` |
| Sun 11/29 | **Write-up, part 2.** Discussion: when the hybrid helps, limitations (gas includes hot water, one zone, mild winter), next steps. | Full draft |
| Mon 11/30 | **Polish and publish.** Remove `draft: true`, run `quarto render` on your Mac (the data is local), delete the example project placeholders, commit `docs/` and `_freeze/`. | Live on GitHub Pages |
| Tue 12/1 | **Done.** Share the link (LinkedIn, resume). | |

### If you fall behind, cut in this order

1. Skip the ML-only baseline (compare physics vs hybrid only).
2. Skip the second and third homes (Building08, Building07).
3. Skip the "what the NN learned" plot.

### Later extensions (not in the 2 weeks)

- Winter 2014/15, after the smart thermostats and radiator valves went in: does the model still work when the controls change?
- 2R2C model (separate air and wall/mass temperatures), using per-room data.
- Repeat on US homes from the ecobee Donate Your Data set (needs a data request).

#| eval: false
from refit_data import load_home, clean_for_model
from rc_model import fit_1r1c

df = clean_for_model(load_home("Building01"))
train = df["2013-11-04":"2013-12-31"]
fit = fit_1r1c(train.t_in.values, train.t_out.values, train.q_heat.values,
               train.i_sol.values, dt_h=0.5, x0=(5.0, 10.0, 5.0))
fit

## Running it locally

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cd projects/rc-thermal-hybrid
python -c "import refit_data as r; r.download_refit(); r.extract_subset()"   # once
python refit_data.py      # coverage table for all 20 homes
python rc_model.py        # synthetic check + first REFIT fit
cd ../.. && quarto preview
```

The site uses `freeze: auto`, so Python code only re-runs when this page changes. GitHub
Pages serves the already-rendered output in `docs/`, so the REFIT data never has to be on GitHub.
